title: Skill signal mapping + manager prep scratchpad
body:
Purpose: quick internal scratch for mapping observable behaviors to promotion/raise signals and to prepare a short, evidence-driven conversation with my manager for the upcoming 1:1. Keep this readable — I want 2–3 crisp stories and 3 asks.

Notes to self (raw):
- Focus on outcomes and measurable impact, not activity. Use numbers where possible (time saved, hires filled, churn %, CSAT).
- Use the 'signal -> evidence -> impact' mini-template below for each anecdote.
- Avoid hedging language in the docs I will read aloud (no 'I think', 'probably'). Use concrete phrasing.

Mini-template for a 60–90s story to share:
1) Signal (what skill/level I'm highlighting).
2) Short context (1 sentence).
3) Action (what I did — 1–2 bullets, active verbs).
4) Outcome (quantified or clear impact).
5) Why it matters for the org/role.

Prepared stories (pick 2–3 to use live):
A) Cross-functional rollout orchestration (signal: influence & project leadership)
- Context: Led onboarding schedule for Dedicated GA with infra, product, and support — 6 teams, 4-week timeline.
- Action: Designed rollout runbook, instituted daily 15-min sync, introduced gating checklist and a post-launch rollback criteria. Owned stakeholder updates.
- Outcome: Met launch date; reduced post-launch incidents by ~40% compared to previous GA; first-week onboarding NPS +12 pts above baseline.
- Why it matters: Shows I can coordinate complex launches with measurable reliability improvements.

B) Cost optimization project (signal: operational rigor & technical curiosity)
- Context: Initiative to reduce per-token cost for high-volume customer cohort.
- Action: Partnered with serving-runtime and infra to test KV cache tweaks and batch configs; prototyped runbook for safe fallbacks.
- Outcome: Estimated 18% reduction in expected monthly spend for two top customers; created a template for future cost pilots.
- Why it matters: Demonstrates ROI-driven experiments that improve unit economics.

C) Manager enablement and hiring lift (signal: coaching, hiring, and scaling teams)
- Context: Helped two new managers ramp during hiring surge.
- Action: Created a 6-week manager enablement checklist, paired for 1:1 calibrations, ran interview calibration sessions (10 hires total).
- Outcome: Time-to-fill improved by ~25% on those roles; new managers reported higher confidence in first 90 days (survey).
- Why it matters: Multiply leader effectiveness; reduces hiring friction.

Evidence bank (quick pointers to cite if asked):
- Launch runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Dedicated-GA-runbook (link in linked_artifacts).
- Cost pilot numbers: JIRA HR-454 (notes and rough calc table).
- Hiring survey summary: slack thread and short spreadsheet (saved as "mgr-ramp-90d.csv").

Key asks (short and specific):
1) Visibility: Ask for a 5–10 minute slot in next skip-level to highlight the Dedicated GA reliability improvements (goal: build cross-org credit and align on next resource needs).
2) Resourcing: Request one IC headcount (contract-to-FTE) for Q3 to own cost-pilot experiments end-to-end. Provide a short business case: expected $X/mo savings vs cost.
3) Calibration: Ask for written feedback on two areas — delegation (where to push down more) and strategic cross-team prioritization.

Risk notes / rebuttals (prep for pushback):
- If core asks on headcount are denied: propose a 3-month scoped contractor with a milestone review and concrete success metrics (cost savings >= 10% for target cohort).
- If manager is skeptical about ROI: offer to run an A/B pilot on a single customer segment with explicit success criteria and a rollback plan.

Framing lines (practice these):
- "The impact I want to highlight is predictable reliability and measurable unit-cost improvements — both enable product teams to ship with confidence and cheaper margins."
- "My goal for next quarter is to institutionalize the cost-pilot process so the org can run repeatable experiments without heavy eng gatekeeping."

Calibration anchors — short phrases to use in calibration conversations:
- "Owns end-to-end outcomes, not just tasks."
- "Builds repeatable playbooks and hands them off."
- "Moves cross-functional projects to low-friction state."

Personal development goals (next 6 months):
- Improve data fluency: run monthly cohort analyses, get comfortable with quick SQL slices for cost and usage signals.
- Delegate more: pick 2 recurring operational tasks to hand off and create an acceptance checklist.
- Strategic influence: get invited to at least 1 product roadmap sync per quarter to surface inference/serving implications earlier.

Quick checklist for the 1:1 (my agenda, 10–12 mins):
- 0:00–1:00: One-sentence priority update.
- 1:00–4:00: Share 2 stories (signal + impact).
- 4:00–7:00: Present asks (visibility, resourcing, calibration).
- 7:00–10:00: Elicit feedback and agree next steps.

Open questions I want answered in the 1:1: list
- Which of these outcomes would you prioritize for sponsorship at the exec level?
- Are there stakeholders I should proactively align with before making a headcount ask?
- Any blind spots you see in my pitch or gaps in evidence?

Next steps (after 1:1):
- If approved to pursue visibility: draft slide (2 slides) and circulate to manager for edits within 48 hours.
- If headcount ok: create a 1-page JD template and cost/benefit summary.
- If pushed back: run scoped 8-week pilot and share weekly micro-updates.

Notes to self (style cues):
- Keep language outcome-focused and crisp.
- Remove any internal jargon before sharing outside people-ops.
- Have exact numbers ready (or clearly labeled estimates).

End of scratchpad.

Recent edits log (for my memory):
- 2026-02-20: added cost-pilot outcome numbers after call with infra.
- 2026-03-02: tightened ask language and added contractor fallback.
- 2026-03-10: finalized agenda and practice lines.
